title: Loan-Level Price Adjustment Grid: Score and Loan-to-Value, Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
Locked rates on the Builder Extended Rate Lock carry a loan-level adjustment for a high loan-to-value, sized by the buyer's qualifying credit score.

**Grid rule.** The confirmation loan-to-value is the loan amount on the lock divided by the Home Purchase Agreement's contract price, as a percent. A confirmation loan-to-value above 85 with a qualifying credit score below 720 adds 0.25 points; a confirmation loan-to-value above 85 with a qualifying credit score of 720 or higher adds 0.125 points; any other lock adds nothing. The points are percentage points of interest rate added to the locked rate before it is held at no less than the par rate and rounded.

| | Qualifying credit score below 720 | Qualifying credit score 720 or higher |
|---|---|---|
| Confirmation loan-to-value above 85 | add 0.25 | add 0.125 |
| Confirmation loan-to-value 85 or below | nothing | nothing |

The loan amount and qualifying credit score are read from the lock record, the contract price from the Home Purchase Agreement record of the agreement the lock finances.

## Cases (hypothetical inputs, contract price USD 400000.00)

- Loan amount USD 344000.00: 86 percent, above 85. Score 690 adds 0.25; score 740 adds 0.125.
- Loan amount USD 340000.00: exactly 85 percent, not above 85; nothing is added whatever the score.
